You have shipped Angular apps for years, and there is still a real chance you are wrong about at least one thing in this article.
I was. Two of the five, actually, and I found out the hard way, in production, on features I had built with total confidence.
These are not obscure edge cases. They are ordinary, everyday Angular mechanics that almost every developer uses constantly and almost nobody was ever taught properly. Read slowly. This one stings a little, in the good way.
Concept 1: What the Banana in a Box Actually Does
The misunderstanding
Most developers use [(ngModel)] for years as one single magic feature, without ever noticing it is two ordinary Angular bindings wearing a trench coat.
<input [(ngModel)]="name">That syntax is shorthand for exactly this.
<input [ngModel]="name" (ngModelChange)="name = $event">A property binding going in, an event binding coming out. Once you see that, an entire category of confusing bugs stops being confusing.
